noi_dung:
Unrelenting Investigation Naturally Brings Enlightenment

The rule for sitting in Chan investigation is: eyes gazing down at the nose, nose contemplating the mouth, mouth contemplating the mind; this checks the scattered mind described as "monkey mind, horse thoughts," keeping the mind from seeking outward. In the Chan Hall, practitioners must not glance east and west—for then the mind chases outer states and no investigation is possible. This demands your special heed! Chan Session time is supremely precious—not a minute or second to waste. Seize the chance to grow wisdom.

Cultivators must not cherish this stinking skin bag. Only parting from that thought can you apply effort; unable to part from it, you become its slave, serving it morning to night. So the true cultivator must regard it as a stinking skin bag—that is, refuse to prize it. Prizing it obstructs the Way. We must "borrow the false to cultivate the true"—treating it only as a means.

In investigating, the great taboo is dozing. Most meditators suffer two common ills: restlessness and sinking—if the mind is not caught in discursive thoughts, it falls into stupor. So in applying effort, throw your whole spirit into investigating—never allowing drowsiness. Once in samadhi, that is another matter.

Chan investigation skill leads to right concentration, right reception—also called samadhi. Realized, this is the state "thus, thus unmoving; clear, ever bright." How to reach it? It takes a bout of bitter effort, transcendent vigor, the mind free of a single discursive thought—until "not a thought arises, the whole appears"—at last seeing your "original face, the homeland scenery."

The key to Chan investigation is the hua-tou. Thought after thought, investigate the hua-tou. Investigate unrelentingly and enlightenment comes of itself—investigating until "mountains end and waters run dry," good news comes of itself, and the state of "bright flowers beneath the willows" appears before your eyes. Someone says: "I have joined so many Chan Sessions—why am I not enlightened?" Because you refuse bitter effort yet keep craving enlightenment. Understand: enlightenment is the fruit of accumulated skill. In time, merit perfected, the moment come—enlightenment comes of itself. With no skill at all, yet wanting enlightenment—that is a deluded idle fancy, no different from "toads craving swan meat"—impossible.
